title: Authority Heatcells & Timeline Flipboard — reimagined RBAC audit + workspace switcher
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, scan-first audit and workspace view that surfaces who has authority at a glance using a novel 'heatcell' grid and an interactive 'timeline flipboard'. The goal is to let engineers and admins quickly triage permission anomalies, evaluate expiring grants, and understand cost/rollout exposure when changing roles without leaving the Console.
background_and_problem: Support teams struggle to answer quick questions: who can perform X, when was that role granted, and which workspace changes increased egress/costs? Existing audit streams are dense and require multiple filters. We want a micro-visual approach that compresses signal (counts, recency, severity) into a grid and pairs it to an explorable timeline to reduce navigation friction.
goals: Make authorization state scannable within 3 seconds for common queries
Surface top 5 anomalous grants per workspace with one click to expand details
Show correlation between role changes and cost spikes (per-route token spend) in the same view
Enable fast actions: revoke, escrow, or schedule expiry from the audit row
acceptance_criteria: Heatcells display workspace x role cells with count, last_granted_date, and severity color
Flipboard timeline expands a selected heatcell to show event stream (grant/modify/revoke) with pagination
Action menu available on each event with links to PRs, Confluence docs, and to initiate an access review
Design includes mobile/adaptive layouts for narrow Console panes
Accessibility contrast and keyboard navigation validated in prototype
design_proposal_summary: Introduce a 3-column layout: left workspace filter + quick-switcher, center 'heatcell' grid where rows=workspaces and columns=role clusters, right 'flipboard' timeline that flips in-place showing the event stream for the selected cell. Heatcells encode three metrics: active_grants (numeric badge), recency (micro-sparkline), and risk (color scale). Flipboard supports inline actions, event grouping by actor, and correlated metric sparklines for cost and latency.
progress_updates: 2026-02-05: Exploratory sketches completed; validated heatcell glyphs with 4 PMs and 2 SREs
2026-02-18: High-fidelity frames in Figma (frames: Heatcell Grid v1, Flipboard Panel v1). Linked in artifacts.
2026-02-25: Design review with Eng (runtime team). Eng flagged event-sourcing perf concern for querying last_30_days per cell; suggested pre-aggregates or streaming cache
2026-03-03: Iterated microcopy for action menu to reduce accidental revokes; added confirmation and 'dry-run' preview

2026-03-10: Prototype user test (5 participants: 3 platform engineers, 2 security owners). All completed common tasks; mean task time 18s to find top anomalous grant — meets scannability goal. Feedback recorded.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use pre-aggregated daily rollups for heatcell metrics rather than live full-scan to keep UI snappy — trades eventual consistency for speed
Limit flipboard event load to 200 items by default with 'load more' to avoid heavy queries — tradeoff: deeper history requires manual expand
Embed correlated cost sparkline at event-group granularity rather than per-event to simplify rendering and reduce network calls
Prefer in-place action menu (revoke/escalate/schedule-expiry) vs modal flows to keep context — added secondary confirm to avoid mistakes
engineering_feedback_and_risks: ENG: Suggest adding a streaming KV cache for recent grants; otherwise expensive joins on audit store will slow console at scale
Risk: RBAC role hierarchies differ across customers (custom role names) — UI needs to fall back to 'role cluster' heuristics
Risk: Correlating cost requires joining audit events with billing logs; offline precompute pipeline agreed as MVP
Performance KPIs: initial render < 400ms for accounts with <= 50 workspaces; paginated queries must return < 200ms
review_feedback: PM (Eloise Vega): Love the quick-switcher; asked for 'owner view' that highlights direct liable users
SRE (Diego Alvarez): Requested throttling guidance and rate-limit UI states; flagged ambiguous error handling on partial data
Legal (Nina Rao): Wants clearer language for actions that export audit slices; noted compliance checklist must be surfaced before export
Design critique (lead): Heatcell color scale needs non-color cues (icons/patterns) for colorblind accessibility
usability_findings: Participants preferred row-major scanning (workspace first) — ensure default sort is by workspace importance
Small screens: flipboard overlay covers too much context; added collapsible heatcell drawer behavior
Action verbs needed clearer differentiation between 'suspend' and 'revoke' — updated copy
compliance_and_security_notes: All export actions must trigger an audit export event and be logged to the customer's audit store
Design includes an 'escrow' flow that marks temporary elevation and auto-expires based on KMS policy
Security review required prior to release — checklist link included in links
next_steps: ENG: Prototype server-side pre-aggregates and expose heatcell summary endpoint (ENG-22108)
Design: Iterate Figma frames with alternative non-color encodings and microcopy for actions
PM: Scope metrics join for cost-correlation and define privacy constraints for cross-workspace joins
Schedule: Usability follow-up with 8 participants including 2 enterprise customers
